summary: I could not refute any identity or capability fact in the Qwen3.5-9B record. The repo is Qwen's own: the HF API gives author Qwen and createdAt 2026-02-27T12:58:26Z, inside the window. License is apache-2.0 and the LICENSE file is Apache 2.0. Safetensors total is 9,653,104,368 params, and the shard sizes add up to 19,306,310,880 bytes. All config.json values match the record: 32 layers, of which 8 are full attention; 4 KV heads; head_dim 256; GDN 16 QK / 32 V heads; max_position_embeddings 262144; untied embeddings; 1 MTP layer; a 27-layer vision tower. The chat template matches the cited lines: tools block at 45-53, XML tool_call replay at 105-127, enable_thinking switch at 149-152. Card line 955 confirms /think and /nothink are not supported. Every benchmark number matches its cited card: Qwen card LCB v6 65.6 (gpt-oss-20b 74.6), BFCL-V4 66.1, TAU2 79.1. Ornith card: SWE-V 53.2, SWE-Pro 31.3, TB2.1 21.3 / 18.9, Toolathlon 29.6. MiMo card: SWE-V 60.0, SWE-Pro 32.0, TB2.1 27.0, Toolathlon 25.9. RedHatAI NVFP4 and FP8 recovery numbers also match. The vLLM v0.33.0 mappings and the vLLM recipe (min_vllm_version 0.17.0, qwen3_coder, qwen3, --language-model-only, YaRN to 1,010,000) are confirmed. Three corrections: (1) The Qwen card does not say its benchmark table was run in thinking mode, so the BFCL 'thinking mode' setting is inferred. (2) The Ornith and MiMo numbers come from model vendors fine-tuning or competing with this model; they are not independent. The MiMo values are said to come from the MiMo-V2.6 technical report, and the MiMo harness is not stated. (3) The Ollama tag list leaves out 9b-mtp-nvfp4 (7.6GB) and 9b-mlx-bf16 (19GB). The card highlight mentions 'sparse Mixture-of-Experts' for the Qwen3.5 family, but this 9B config has no experts, and the recipe says dense, so 'Dense' stands. I did not re-check the llama.cpp, memory-arithmetic or speed claims. Raw files are in $SCRATCH/fc95/.
